lineage: fidelity probe p04_colours, 2026-09-24 (promoted by WP-G G-2, 2026-09-25)
notes: Finding F5 (modern colour functions, docs/engine/fidelity/01-FINDINGS.md): tinted fills written every way a
model writes them - hex, rgba, color-mix (srgb, and oklab with transparent), oklch, hsl, 8-digit hex,
color(display-p3), a gradient of color-mix, rgb(... / 8%) - and text coloured by color-mix and oklch on dark
boxes, plus a color-mix banner with a var() left edge. Before the paint package (E) every modern function came
back null: fills vanished and the text went black. paint.html carries the modern syntaxes in isolation; this
family keeps the probe's side-by-side control (swatch 1) and the alpha forms (2, 4, 7, 10), which paint does not.
The HTML is the probe's but for one line: the heading has width:872px, to layout-06's title zone's right edge (see
flexgrid's notes; here the probe's title overhung by 3 px through the test masters' manifest/theme mismatch).
text 14 = title 1 + 12 swatch texts + banner 1. A swatch whose <b> (display:block) is followed by loose text
is 1 element of 2 paragraphs - the block and the anonymous run stack (1, 2, 3, 11, 12); the others are 1
paragraph. The banner's inline <b> and the text after it are 1 paragraph of 2 runs.
shape 14 = 12 swatch roundRects (6 px radius, each with its uniform 1 px BBBBBB border as the stroke) + the
banner's roundRect fill + its 6 px left border (a per-side border is its own shape, 1E9E5A from var(--accent)).
Fill values, measured on the merged engine (E's color.js normaliser): 1 E3F4EA; 2 1E9E5A alpha 0.12;
3 E4F3EB (= 0.12 x 1E9E5A + 0.88 x FFFFFF); 4 0B5CAD alpha 0.1 (mixing with transparent keeps the colour and
scales alpha); 5 DCF7E1; 6 E7F9F0; 7 1E9E5A alpha 0.12 (0x1F / 255); 8 E1F8EA; 9 a linear gradient
CEDEEF -> FFFFFF at 90 degrees (the first stop = 0.2 x 0B5CAD + 0.8 x FFFFFF); 10 0B5CAD alpha 0.08;
banner E9F5EE. Text runs: 11 DADEE3 (= 0.85 x FFFFFF + 0.15 x 0B2545), 12 F8F8F8 (oklch(0.98 0 0)); every
other run 1D2433.
Diagnostics: swatch 9's gradient is interpolated in oklab by the browser and in sRGB by PowerPoint, so E
reports it as approximated (info). Lint: three info colour-gamut findings, one per colour written in a
wide-gamut space - oklch() fill (5), color(display-p3) fill (8), oklch() text (12); color-mix(in oklab ...)
is not matched because its result is sRGB.
